themes_detail.label: Litter Crisis Exploding
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests spiked to 10 complaints THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 567% increase (z-score: 12.02)—signaling either a sudden waste management breakdown or aggressive new littering in CD108 that residents can no longer tolerate.
evidence: 10 litter basket complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (567% spike, z-score: 12.02)
Concurrent spike in commercial disposal complaints: 5 THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 baseline (900% increase, z-score: 9.0)
Concurrent spike in dumpster complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 baseline (700% increase, z-score: 5.42)
reporting_angles: Interview Sanitation Department about resource allocation or service cuts in the UES this week
Canvass residents on Madison/Park/5th Ave to pinpoint where litter complaints are concentrated and why they're spiking now
Investigate whether new construction (1,940 DOB filings in 90 days, 1,747 alterations) is generating excess waste without proper disposal

themes_detail.label: Dead Trees Sudden Surge
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints jumped to 5 in the past week compared to a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1900% spike (z-score: 10.97)—raising questions about whether disease, weather, or deferred maintenance has suddenly accelerated tree loss on the Upper East Side.
evidence: 5 dead/dying tree complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1900% spike, z-score: 10.97)
Parks Department baseline shows chronic underinvestment in tree maintenance across CD108
Long-standing community board budget request for infrastructure upgrades suggests systemic tree maintenance gaps
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department to determine if a specific pathogen, pest, or weather event is killing trees this week
Map the 5 complaints to see if tree loss is concentrated in a particular neighborhood or park
Examine whether aging infrastructure (many UES buildings pre-1950) and limited street tree budget correlate with sudden die-off

themes_detail.label: Commercial Waste Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Commercial disposal complaints shot to 5 THIS WEEK from a 0.5 baseline—a 900% surge (z-score: 9.0)—mirroring the litter and dumpster spikes and suggesting commercial establishments or contractors are violating waste management rules.
evidence: 5 commercial disposal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (900% increase, z-score: 9.0)
Dumpster complaints also up 700% THIS WEEK (3 vs. 0.4 baseline), suggesting connected waste handling problem
Vendor enforcement complaints remain elevated at 389 total over 90 days, indicating ongoing commercial district tension
reporting_angles: Obtain 311 complaint locations to identify which commercial corridors (Madison Ave, Lexington, etc.) are generating most violations
Interview Sanitation Enforcement about whether they've deployed additional officers or are aware of a specific commercial operator causing problems
Investigate whether the 1,747 active alteration permits are generating construction debris disposal violations

themes_detail.label: Boiler Complaints Rise Sharply
themes_detail.summary: Boiler complaints tripled THIS WEEK to 3 complaints versus a 0.8 baseline (300% increase, z-score: 5.2), coinciding with the ongoing heat/hot water crisis (1,013 complaints over 90 days) and suggesting heating system failures may be accelerating as winter approaches.
evidence: 3 boiler complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (300% increase, z-score: 5.2)
Heat/hot water remains top complaint category over 90 days with 1,013 total complaints
Long-standing community board budget request for 'renovate or upgrade public housing developments' (NYCHA) suggests systemic heating infrastructure failures
reporting_angles: Interview HPD about whether boiler inspections are revealing systemic failures in older UES buildings
Contact NYCHA about heating system readiness at public housing developments (Lincoln, Jefferson, Lexington Houses) heading into winter
Determine if the boiler spike is concentrated in rent-stabilized or NYCHA buildings where maintenance may be deferred

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dogs Spike
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK from a 0.4 baseline—a 700% spike (z-score: 5.42)—indicating either a sudden increase in irresponsible pet owners or inadequate park enforcement on the UES.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% increase, z-score: 5.42)
No concurrent increase in animal control or dog park-related 311 complaints, suggesting isolated incident or park-specific problem
UES contains multiple dog-friendly parks (Central Park, Carl Schurz Park) where enforcement may be declining
reporting_angles: Ask Parks Department if there have been staffing changes or reduced enforcement at major UES parks this week
Geo-locate the 3 complaints to identify if they cluster around one park or corridor
Interview dog owners in high-complaint areas to understand why compliance is dropping
